method: s265 (wolf-lang#918). bench-gates builds corpus/hello.lu on the release tier with the gauntlet's own driver (target/debug/wolf --release --no-cache) and bench/startup/hello.c with the host's clang -O2, traces each once with `strace -qq -o` in an empty environment (LD_LIBRARY_PATH would add loader probes, two libraries' worth for wolf and one for C), and counts the system calls from the one after execve to exit_group (exit lines excluded). The wolf count minus the C count is the runtime's own start-up and exit; the dynamic loader's calls appear in both. Gated: may not rise above this number; `cargo xtask bench-gates --record` ratchets it down. The wall half (50 interleaved starts of each, the medians and the ratio) is printed report-only.
recorded: kasumi, s265, ubuntu:24.04 container (glibc 2.39, clang 18.1.3), linux 7.2.8: wolf 47 calls, C 35. For scale, the published release archives' hello counted the same way: 0.2.34 42 calls (7 over C), 0.2.35 59 (24 over C); s265's eager direct read of the main stack's bounds 51 (16); the guard resolved at the first fault 47 (12).
floor_method: The floor rows (bench-gates' floor_rows) read the same two hellos, linked as the syscall row's are against the release runtime archive, at each one's exit stop with address randomisation off (bench/startup/exitstop.c, built with the host's clang -O2), 21 reads of each, interleaved, and take the medians: floor_hello_minus_c_vmhwm_kb (VmHWM, wolf minus C, gated at the record plus 64 kB, one fault-around window), floor_hello_minus_c_minflt (minor faults, wolf minus C, the record plus 3) and floor_hello_text_pages (the hello's own r-x pages resident, the record plus 2). The alternate-stack row reads how much of the main thread's 32 KiB alternate stack a main-thread overflow writes (bench/startup/overflow.lu, the native tier), by filling the stack with a pattern at the exec stop and finding the lowest byte changed at the exit stop, and gates only that it is never more than half the stack: the stack has no guard below it. The byte count is printed report-only, beside the kernel's AT_MINSIGSTKSZ and the difference, and has no record: it differs between hosts (5960 and 7944 bytes on two hosted runners, 7816 in a container on another machine), and AT_MINSIGSTKSZ is the largest signal frame the kernel could push, not the one it pushed (11952 on the second runner, more than everything written; 3632 in the container), so the report's own share cannot be told apart. A host that refuses address randomisation off or the trace fails these rows by name. A floor key that is absent reads REPORT-ONLY and fails bench-gates, so no run is green while one is unset; `--record` on the gate's host writes them.
